changelog: Inserted a fallback ordering rule into [Order Principles] that prefers cuts which keep a verb/auxiliary together with its required object/complement over cuts that split the verb from that complement — to address the primary finding that the prompt currently favors earlier splits that strand verbs or complements.
findings: When two candidate cuts are both allowed, the prompt prefers earlier splits that leave verbs or complements stranded instead of preserving verb+object; the prompt should prefer cuts that keep a verb with its required complement.
The prompt allows cuts that leave a clause or predicate syntactically incomplete by separating it from a required complement or reason clause, which yields high contradiction and kills the set.

edits.now: When one candidate splits a verb (or auxiliary) from its required object/complem

diagnosis.why: The new fallback ordering rule kept verbs/auxiliaries with their complements, shifting preferred cuts away from verb-complement splits; that helped deeper/long-budget positions slightly (≤99) but reduced agreement at the top ranks and hurt short-latency bins (≤3, ≤5, ≤7) by forcing cuts into noun compounds and internal phrase boundaries instead of the earlier verb splits.
diagnosis.lesson: Do not let a fallback that protects verb–complement adjacency override constraints that prevent splitting tight noun compounds or internal phrase material, because that tradeoff improves long-budget rank depth at the cost of short-latency quality.
